control_flow: avoidWalls: if the right light is below 60 %, then check obstacles, else call driveInTheDark.
Obstacle check: if the front sensor sees something, turn left 15°; else if the left sensor sees something, turn right 15°; else call driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if the left light is below 70 %, drive forward; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if the front sensor sees something, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Inside a dark tunnel, turn right when a wall is close on the left and left when one is close on the right, so it gets through a bending tunnel without touching the walls.

scenarios.title: Gets through a tunnel that bends to the right
assumptions: The robot starts in the dark part of the tunnel; on a plain floor it would curve away instead of entering it.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It turns right away from the left wall and gets through the tunnel without touching it.

scenarios.coded_response: It turns left 15° each time the front sensor sees the wall.

scenarios.trigger: The front sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.title: A wall straight ahead in the dark tunnel
assumptions: You didn't say what to do with a wall straight ahead; the program turns left.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It turns left so it doesn't drive into the wall.

scenarios.coded_response: It follows the line and, when the front sensor sees the wall, it stops.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts in bright light on a black line, heading along it, with a wall across the line ahead.
scenarios.trigger: It follows the line, then the wall comes in front.
scenarios.title: In bright light it follows a line and stops at a wall
assumptions: You only spoke about the dark tunnel; outside it the program follows a line and stops at walls.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line and stops in front of the wall.

uncertainties: The two light sensors sit at the same depth, so they read the same brightness: the right-light check only matters once the robot is more than about 10 cm inside the tunnel.
The program reads the left and front obstacle sensors but not the right one, so it may not see a wall close on the right as you described.
Turning left when a wall is straight ahead can steer the robot into the wall in a bend, so the 'turns left' result may not get it through.
You didn't say what the robot should do in bright light; that scenario is inferred from the program.
